text:
sam: heads-up - ran perf + flamegraph on a repro where tail latency doubled when prefetcher is turned on. attaching notes.
jia: interesting, was that on ded10? what kernel selection was used?
sam: ded10 GPU box but this is CPU-side bottleneck during tokenization/scheduler handoff. kernel selector picked fallback path (vec-quant) because seq_len distribution widened.
mike: can you paste the perf top snippet?
sam: sure:

```
# perf top -p <pid> -n 30
  15.2%  python  PyObject_Call
  12.7%  runtime  scheduler_run
  11.1%  libtoken  tokenize_fastpath
   9.3%  libc     __memcpy_avx_unaligned_erms
   6.0%  python  _PyEval_EvalFrameDefault
```
jia: scheduler_run at 12.7% feels high. Did you do flamegraph on stack samples to see call chains?
sam: yes — flame shows deep stacks where tokenize_fastpath -> memcpy -> scheduler_run; looks like prefetch threads are causing more context switching.
elaine: kv-cache metrics? could be more misses causing extra work
sam: KV hit-rate before prefetch ON: 94.6% ; after prefetch ON: 91.2% (5% absolute drop). That lines up with extra tokenizer work.
mike: small miss bump -> more long-lived KV lookups? or locks around kvcache eviction?
jia: any lock contention in perf report?
sam: perf record + perf script showed heavy time in a spinlock in kvcache.c:evict_slot. snippet:
```
# perf script | grep evict_slot | head
sample: evict_slot+0x24/0x90
sample: evict_slot+0x24/0x90
...
```
mike: so two factors: scheduling churn due to prefetch threads + evict lock contention. Combined amplifies Python scheduler overhead.
elaine: how reproducible is the latency regression?
sam: reproducible on scale test: p95 goes from 180ms -> 370ms when prefetch thread count >= 4 for that workload.
jia: what's batching behavior during those runs? are we accidentally increasing small-batch flush frequency?
sam: yes, batching tuner logs show average batch size drops from 16 to 9 after prefetch ON. Seems prefetch injects extra small requests causing early flush.
mike: can we try 1) increase kvcache capacity by 20% 2) switch prefetch to async-no-block 3) bump batching hold-time by 5ms and retest
sam: ran quick tests:
- kvcache +20% -> p95 290ms
- prefetch async-no-block -> p95 210ms
- hold-time +5ms -> p95 195ms
combination -> p95 175ms (back to baseline)
jia: great. any kernel selection change required?
sam: none. the root is workload shape + prefetch semantics + small-batch churn exposing kvcache eviction spinlock.
elaine: action items?
sam: 1) change prefetch default to async-no-block behind flag (infra rollout) 2) tune kvcache default capacity heuristic for short sequences 3) add a batching metric: batch-size tail by route and prefetch flag 4) perf test on ded10 CI with these three changes
mike: I'll own the infra rollout flag
jia: I'll add batching metric and tweak capacity heuristic
elaine: I'll schedule CI perf job for ded10
infra-bot: deploy flag created: rollout/prefetch-async-no-block -> 0% (canary pipeline queued)
sam: I'll prepare a short doc with perf commands and flame images (will drop into /confluence later). thanks all :thumbsup:
